## [2026-07-31] correction+reports | BOOK RECUT ON THE LIVE CADENCE (user: "recoupe le backtest et le monte carlo sur la cadence live"). While implementing it I found my previous-turn attribution was WRONG and incomplete: the gap between the exploratory IBS loop and the deployed driver is not one artefact (same-bar re-entry) but **three**, all from the loop running its entry test AFTER the exit block of the same bar and testing the exit on the CURRENT bar instead of the last closed one: (a) it can re-enter on the very bar a stop fired, filling at that bar's OPEN = a price already in the past; (b) it NEVER tests the exit on the entry bar (it enters at the bottom of that iteration), so a signal exit needs >=2 bars while the driver, seeing the entry bar close at the next rollover, can exit after ONE; (c) it resolves the stop of bar t before considering an entry on bar t. My first fix (a `same_bar_reentry` flag) only covered (a) and produced 303 trades vs the driver's 302 with 269 mismatched rows -> discarded. REPLACED by an explicit `run_ibs(..., cadence=...)`: **"live" (new DEFAULT)** = one decision per daily-bar rollover on the last CLOSED bar, filling at the new bar's open = literally what `NasIbsStrategy.step` does; **"literal"** = the original exp-009 loop, kept ONLY so `verify` can prove the live signal math reproduces it (still 314/314 exact). Verified the live cadence reproduces the driver replay trade-for-trade. Also checked a 4th suspected difference — the driver `return`s after an exit so it cannot exit-and-enter in the same pass — and it costs **0 trades / 0.0 R** over the whole history (a 30-bar time-exit never coincides with IBS<0.2), so the driver was left unchanged. | RECUT BOOK (canonical, `build_reports.py`): IBS brick **+5.64 -> +4.81 R/yr** (n 300->287, t 4.77->**5.16**, PF 1.99->**2.21**, still 8/9 +yrs — the edge is STRONGER on the live cadence, only the R/yr was optimistic).
